chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'dan, from Al-Husayn ibn Ayman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'O Husayn! Spend and have certainty in the Replacement from Allah, for neither will a slave nor a maid be stingy with expenditure regarding what Pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that they would end up spending in what Angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic'.

key_terms.الْخَلَف: Replacement or substitute provided by God

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of being stingy with spending for Allah's pleasure according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links charitable expenditure directly to divine compensation (khalf), emphasizing that stinginess in righteous causes leads to the loss of that wealth in ways displeasing to Allah. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'spending' not merely as charity, but as a spiritual investment where the believer trusts Allah to replace what is given for His sake. The warning against miserliness underscores the principle that wealth is a trust, and hoarding it for non-righteous purposes results in its eventual dissipation.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Sa’dan, from Al Husayn Bin Ayman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘O Husayn! Spend and have certainty in the Replacement from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for neither will a slave nor a maid be stingy with expenditure regarding what Pleases Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, except that they would end up spending in what Angers Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid has narrated from Jahm ibn al-Hakam al-Mad’iniy from Isma‘il ibn abu Ziyad who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, There are three kinds of hands: the asking hand, the withholding hand, and the spending hand, of which the best hand is the spending hand.’”
